::: {#sol-autograd-descent}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
learning_rate = 4.0
theta = torch.tensor(0.0, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
for step in range(100):
    (slope,) = torch.autograd.grad(mean_log_loss(theta), theta)
    with torch.no_grad():
        theta -= learning_rate * slope
theta_descent = theta.item()
(final_slope,) = torch.autograd.grad(mean_log_loss(theta), theta)

cutoffs = np.arange(0, 16.005, 0.01)
grid_step = cutoffs[1] - cutoffs[0]
with torch.no_grad():
    grid_loss = [mean_log_loss(torch.tensor(c)).item() for c in cutoffs]
theta_grid = cutoffs[np.argmin(grid_loss)]
gap = abs(theta_descent - theta_grid)
print(theta_descent, final_slope.item(), theta_grid, gap)
```

[Gradient descent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#the-algorithm) ends at $\param$ = `r sprintf("%.4f", py$theta_descent)`,
where the slope is `r format(py$final_slope$item(), digits = 2)`,
and the grid's lowest point is at `r sprintf("%.2f", py$theta_grid)`,
the cutoff found in [the review's solution](ml-review.qmd#sol-smooth-loss).
The two differ by `r sprintf("%.4f", py$gap)`,
`r if (py$gap < py$grid_step) "less" else "more"` than the grid's spacing of `r py$grid_step`.

The update runs inside `torch.no_grad()`,
which tells PyTorch not to record it:
the step is a change to $\param$, not part of the loss.
Without it, PyTorch would record the in-place subtraction on `theta`,
and it raises an error for a recorded in-place change to a [tensor](#def-tensor) that was created with `requires_grad=True`.

:::
